messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed tenants' warmup after eviction spikes can cause double-allocation bursts. proposing a lightweight safety handshake: per-tenant prewarm budget + rollback path if warming causes backpressure. sketch below.

sam: can you sketch the flow? is this host-local only or cross-node warmup too?

maria: host-local first. flow: eviction frees pages -> warmup controller schedules prefetches for async warming -> if prefetches push host into stall or exceed budget we trigger rollback: mark warmed pages as deferred and restore resident snapshot. key is to avoid oscillation.

liam: so admission + budget enforcement. what's the rollback signal? time window, rate, or explicit stalls?

maria: mix of signals. counters we track: prefetch_tokens, bytes_warmed, stall_incidents. rollback if bytes_warmed > budget OR stall_incidents > threshold within window. want simple defaults: 256MB, 1s window, stall_threshold=3. example config: 

```
warmup:
  budget_tokens: 256MB
  window_ms: 1000
  stall_threshold: 3
  rollback_action: snapshot+defer
```

anya: fair — but how do we keep big tenants from hogging the warmup budget?

maria: allocate warmup share proportional to commit size but with a hard per-tenant cap. also tie global multiplier to cluster load: if cluster_load > 0.8 then warmup_multiplier *= 0.5. admission controller enforces at enqueue time.

chris: race concern: rollback will reintroduce freed pages — won't the evictor immediately pick them again and recreate the loop?

maria: we mitigate with two mechanisms: 1) a soft-protect TTL bit placed on rollback pages (e.g. 2s) to prevent immediate eviction; 2) apply a temporary hotness penalty so the evictor deprioritizes those pages. combined with controlled async warming queue this prevents tight loops.

sam: any hot-path perf regs? adding counters and penalty updates might be expensive.

maria: keep hot path minimal — single atomic per-tenant token decrement, and bitmap toggles off the critical fast-path. heavier accounting (percentiles, telemetry) is asynchronous. microbench shows no meaningful p99 change, ~2% throughput loss at extreme synthetic prefetching.

chris: can we simulate with existing alloc tracer and evictor test harness?

maria: yes, I ran end-to-end on my dev box with trace toggles. results look sane. plan: open RFC followup with API sketch, config knobs, and telemetry. telemetry to include: warmup_budget_used, warmup_rollbacks, soft_protect_hits, prefetch_requeues.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for runtime/warmup-v2 passed on canary-3.

anya: ok — please open the RFC followup and include a simple state machine diagram + failure modes. also add a perf gate for 1% throughput regressions. :thumbsup: 

maria: will do. thanks everyone.
